public_rationale: The ordinary present-tense reading is supported. Contemporary disclosures and research document unreliable outputs, enormous training corpora, acquisition pressure, remaining interpretability barriers, and failures on changed reasoning tasks. Interpretability research also showed useful progress. The evidence supports continuing limitations, not a claim that every model was wholly opaque or that generalization could never improve.
limitations: The result depends on reading 'never complete' within the surrounding observation about contemporary systems.
The examples establish real limitations but do not measure their prevalence across every generative model.
Acquisition pressure relies on investigative reporting rather than publicly inspectable internal company records.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI today suffers from brittleness (unreliability), greed for data, opacity, and shallow, never-complete generalization.

statement.excerpt: Fast forward six years, and those problems are exactly what is ailing GenAI today: the brittleness (a term for unreliability); the greed for data that is causing the desperation that the Times described; the opacity (uninterpretability) that makes debugging, fairness, and engineering so hard; and the shallowness, meaning that generalizations are never complete.

from_speaker: causing the desperation that the Times described
makes debugging, fairness, and engineering so hard
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that these were substantial, continuing limitations of contemporary generative AI, not that every system failed every task.

I read incomplete generalization as failures to transfer learned capabilities reliably to changed situations. The surrounding word 'today' makes this an observation, not a proof that future systems can never generalize.
I use early 2024 through publication as the current reporting period for these continuously evaluated systems. There is no standard quarterly reporting cycle for their technical limitations.
Data hunger means large training-data requirements and pressure to acquire additional material. Desperation describes the documented acquisition pressure, not a measurable psychological state.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous evaluations and disclosures establish recurring unreliability, substantial data requirements and acquisition pressure, consequential interpretability limitations, and failures to generalize across changed tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence establishes that one or more of these alleged continuing limitations had been broadly overcome, or that the reported data-acquisition pressure was unrelated to training-data requirements.

evidence.locator: Opening discussion of the image-generation failure
evidence.explanation: Google documented inaccurate outputs and inappropriate refusals in its deployed Gemini image feature. This supports the claim of consequential unreliability.
The report discloses trillion-token training corpora for contemporary models. This establishes large data consumption, though corpus size alone does not establish acquisition pressure.

evidence.publisher: Samuel Marks and colleagues, via arXiv
evidence.explanation: The paper connects interpretability difficulties to practical model analysis and editing, and acknowledges remaining opaque components. It also demonstrates useful circuit discovery and debiasing, qualifying any suggestion that interpretation or engineering was impossible.

evidence.publisher: Martha Lewis and Melanie Mitchell, via arXiv
evidence.explanation: Three GPT models performed substantially worse on altered analogy problems while human performance remained high. This supports incomplete generalization in the tested systems and tasks.

evidence.locator: Opening section, following the account of YouTube transcription
evidence.publisher: The New York Times, syndicated by The Indian Express
evidence.explanation: The investigation describes then-current acquisition pressure and connects it to training-data demand, drawing on interviews and internal records. Its earlier examples are not treated as new April events; the syndicated publication is within the evaluation cutoff.
